theme: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

reports.title: Margaret Sales
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: I attach the latest audit on medical records carried out across the Trust's wards. The wards involved were Oxborough and Marham for the admission in question. With medical record completion, action taken is taken on a regular basis and I set out the detail of this process below.
promises.summary: Audit medical records regularly to ensure completion

concerns.quote: Records were not always completed as required
Nurses had difficulty in contacting front line on call medical staff on two occasions

reports.title: Bonnie Webster: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: In my role as Acting Chief Executive Officer of The Queen Elizabeth Hospital King's Lynn NHS Foundation Trust I now set out the Trust's responses to the three concerns you raised in box (5) of the report.
promises.summary: Addresses concerns about communication and response

concerns.quote: The evidence of Mr and Mrs Webster is they were unaware of the seriousness of the situation. Caesarian Section was discussed but was not advised or recommended at the meeting at 06.50 hours. This was clearly a traumatic meeting and Mr and Mrs Webster were upset which would have impacted on their ability to understand and take in important information. In such a situation clear language and ensuring an understanding of the whole situation is paramount
concerns.hazard: lack of clear communication about caesarean section

concerns.quote: Antiobiotics were prescribed at the initial review meeting at 09.35 hours. These were not given until 12.30 hours
Evidence was heard that staff alerted the paediatric team on foot, rather than using the emergency
concerns.hazard: staff alerted paediatric team via foot instead of emergency system

links.explanation: Both reports highlight problems with the hospital's bleep system for contacting on‑call medical staff. The earlier report notes nurses could not reach staff despite bleeps being issued; the later report shows staff bypassing the bleep system altogether.
links.earlier_quote: Nurses had difficulty in contacting front line on call medical staff on two occasions.
links.later_quote: Evidence was heard that staff alerted the paediatric team on foot, rather than using the emergency "bleep" system
